problem_statement: themefisher/godocs-bulma is a runnable Gulp-built static documentation site (source/*.html assembled from gulp-file-include partials + Bulma SCSS, compiled to theme/). It ships a consistent docs design system: shared masthead partials (source/partials/blocks/navigation-home.htm and navigation-inner.htm) whose anchors carry a shared nav-link class, a Bulma type scale, and a shared footer partial, all included on every page. Long articles such as source/single.html carry many headings (Emphasis, Links, Lists, Notices, Tabs, Tables) but readers have no quick way to jump between them and no signal of where they are. Add an on-brand "On this page" section quick-nav to the docs so readers can jump between the article's sections. Build it as a SHARED partial (source/partials/blocks/section-nav.htm) styled in the SCSS so it renders identically on the Home overview (source/index.html), the inner list page (source/list.html) and the article page (source/single.html) - a real cross-page docs surface, not a one-off. The strip shows an "On this page" eyebrow, a horizontal row of section chips (Overview, Emphasis, Links, Lists, Notices, Tabs, Tables) each carrying the shared nav-link class, and a live "Reading: <section>" readout. Clicking a chip must mark it active AND update the readout to the clicked section (Reading: Notices), re-reading the live active chip rather than a value snapshotted once at setup. The chip row must wrap on 390px mobile so the page has no horizontal overflow, the active chip must stay legible (high-contrast, on the GoDocs green system - not a pale-on-pale blob), and the eyebrow must sit clear of the chip row without collision. Do NOT ship a rigid fixed-width chip row that overflows mobile, an off-system slate/pale recolor of the active chip, a strip that only renders on one page, or a readout frozen on the initial section while the chip highlight moves.
required_content: Add a shared "On this page" section quick-nav partial (source/partials/blocks/section-nav.htm) rendered from the SCSS design system so it appears identically on the Home overview, the inner list page and the article page - a real cross-page docs surface.

The strip shows an "On this page" eyebrow, a horizontal row of section chips (Overview, Emphasis, Links, Lists, Notices, Tabs, Tables) each carrying the shared nav-link class, and a live "Reading: <section>" readout.
Clicking a section chip marks it active and updates the readout to the clicked section (e.g. Reading: Notices) by re-reading the live active chip, not a value snapshotted once at setup.
The chip row wraps on 390px mobile so the strip and page stay free of horizontal overflow, and the active chip stays legible on the GoDocs green system with the eyebrow clear of the chip row.
Keep the existing docs content (the single.html article, the Home overview, the shared masthead and footer) intact.

change_completion: A shared "On this page" section quick-nav strip is added as source/partials/blocks/section-nav.htm and rendered on the Home overview, the inner list page and the article page with an eyebrow, section chips (Overview..Tables) and a live "Reading: <section>" readout.
Each section chip carries the shared nav-link class and links to the matching article heading anchor.
design_consistency: The strip reuses the GoDocs green brand system, the Bulma type scale and the shared chrome so it is visually part of the docs, and it renders on every doc page rather than only one.
The active section chip stays high-contrast/legible on the green system and the eyebrow sits clear of the chip row with no collision or clipping.
responsive: The section-chip row wraps on 390px mobile so the strip and the page have no horizontal overflow at the standard tolerance.
The strip holds its layout across desktop, tablet and mobile viewports on the article page.
regression: The existing single.html article content, the Home overview and the shared masthead/footer chrome remain intact.
No off-system standalone page or bespoke inline layout replaces the shared design-system chrome.

design_constraints: Build the section quick-nav as a shared partial styled in the SCSS system, reusing the GoDocs green theme, the Bulma typography type scale, the shared card/chip pattern, pill spacing and border radius, not a bespoke inline-styled one-off block.
Render the strip on the Home overview, the inner list page and the article page so it is a real cross-page docs surface with a consistent layout, not a single-page decoration.
Keep the section-chip row responsive: it must wrap on 390px mobile so the strip never forces horizontal overflow, preserving the mobile layout and spacing.
Keep the active chip legible and high-contrast on the green theme (never pale-on-pale) with the eyebrow spacing clear of the chip row, so the visual style stays consistent with the docs.
Wire the "Reading: <section>" readout to re-read the live active chip on every click so it always names the clicked section, never a value snapshotted once at setup.

Do not introduce off-system styling (a fixed-width nowrap chip row that overflows mobile, an off-brand slate or pale-mint active chip, an eyebrow colliding with the chips) or remove content from the existing pages.
state_constraints: desktop_single verifies the article page renders the shared "On this page" strip through the design system: the section chips (Overview..Tables) carry the shared nav-link class and the live "Reading:" readout is present, and the original article content is intact.
mobile_single verifies the section-chip row wraps at 390px so the article page has no horizontal overflow and the strip stays legible.
desktop_single_notices verifies that clicking the Notices chip updates the readout to "Reading: Notices" (the readout follows the live active chip, not a snapshot).

desktop_initial and desktop_list verify the shared section quick-nav renders on the Home overview and the inner list page too - the strip is a consistent cross-page docs surface, not present on only one page.
author_notes: Add an on-brand "On this page" section quick-nav to the themefisher/godocs-bulma Gulp documentation site as a shared partial (source/partials/blocks/section-nav.htm) rendered from the SCSS design system on the Home overview (index.html), the inner list page (list.html) and the article page (single.html). The reference strip shows an "On this page" eyebrow, a wrapping row of GoDocs-green section chips carrying the shared nav-link class (Overview, Emphasis, Links, Lists, Notices, Tabs, Tables) and a live "Reading: <section>" readout wired in source/js/onpage-nav.js to re-read the live active chip on click. INFRA (identical across reference, baseline and bad, NOT part of the task content): the section-nav partial markup, the shared onpage-nav SCSS import in source/scss/style.scss, the .jshintrc used by the gulp jshint task, and loading source/js/onpage-nav.js from the shared footer partial. The baseline keeps the site's original rigid layout defect (a fixed-width nowrap chip row that overflows 390px mobile and an off-brand slate active chip) and only mounts the strip on the article page, so it fails responsive, visual and cross-page checks while its readout wiring stays correct. The bad solution mounts a "smart wrong" strip whose active chip is a pale-mint-on-pale-mint illegible blob with the eyebrow collapsed onto the clipped chip row, omits the strip from the list page, and freezes the readout on the initial section (a stale closure snapshot) so clicking a chip toggles the highlight but never updates "Reading:". Assets referenced: the shared logo.png masthead image and the article getting-started.jpg imagery render unchanged on every leg.
